To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cyclodextrine molecules are toroids with a thickness of the solvent layer of 0.4–0.5 nm, the hydrodynamic radius of cyclodextrine molecule is in a range of 0.5–0.6 nm, the friction coefficient of cyclodextrins is 1–2 nm ^{−2}, the diffusion coefficient of cyclodextines is 1.2–3.0 × 10 ^{−10}
cyclodextrin (CD) molecules are characterized by a very high axial ratio, a very low frictional ratio, and a low sedimentation coefficient.
cyclodextrin solutions in aqueous solvents are characterized by the formation of toroids with a diameter of about 2.5 nm and a thickness of the solvent layer of 1.5–2.0 nm, depending on the solvent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new analytical methods for the characterization of cyclodextrins in solution and with the determination of the molecular properties of these molecules.
a detailed study of the hydrodynamics of the cyclodextins.
the determination of the hydrodynamic characteristics of cyclodextrins in dilute solutions and the interpretation of the experimental results by means of theoretical calculations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the hydrodynamic properties of the three investigated cyclodextrin derivatives are very similar, and that their hydrodynamic behavior in dilute solutions is mainly determined by the size and shape of the molecule.
cyclodextrins are toroids with an inner cavity and two outer solvent layers.
the hydrodynamic properties of the cyclodextrans are determined by their molecular shape.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thickness of the water layers on the surface is about 0.7 nm.
the cyclodextrim molecule is a torus with a diameter of about 1.5 nm and an average thickness of the solvent layer on the surface of about 1 nm.

the hydrodynamic behavior of the cyclodextrans in dilute solutions can be described by a rigid toroidal model with a solvent layer of thickness between 0.4 nm and 0.6 nm on the surface of the molecules.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the hydrodynamic properties of cyclotetrasaccharides are similar to those of cyclodextrins, which are widely used in the pharmaceutical, chemical, and food industries, and can be used in the same applications as cyclodextrins.
cyclodextrin hydrodynamic properties can be successfully used for the estimation of the size of the cyclodexrin cavity and the thickness of the water layers on the surface.
the hydrodynamic properties of cyclotetradecatrime are very similar to the hydrodynamic properties observed for the cyclodextrim family.
